Detailed method

The calculator opens at 400 g flour, 52% hydration, 1.5% salt, and 0.4% yeast. That is 208 g water, 6 g salt, and 1.6 g yeast, 615.6 g of dough. The balls fields open at 4 sheets of 153.9 g. Roll them nearly paper thin and bake them until they blister. Stack the sheets while they are warm if you want them soft, or leave them until they dry if you want crisp crackers. These times assume you only change the flour amount and keep the percentages the same. Still judge the dough by how it looks and feels.

  1. Mix Stir 400 g flour, 208 g water, 6 g salt, and 1.6 g instant yeast, then knead for 6 to 8 minutes until smooth. At 52% the dough is stiff. Aim for about 24°C (75°F).
  2. Bulk Cover it at about 24°C (75°F) for 90 to 120 minutes. With 0.4% yeast it should grow by about half.
  3. Divide Divide the 615.6 g dough into 4 pieces of 153.9 g, the weight in the balls fields. Roll each into a smooth ball, cover, and rest 15 minutes.
  4. Roll Dust the counter lightly. Roll each ball as thin as you can, about 30 cm across, nearly paper thin. If it snaps back, rest 5 minutes and roll again. A thick spot stays pale and soft.
  5. Heat Heat a stone, steel, or a dry heavy skillet as hot as the oven will go, about 250°C (480°F), for 20 minutes.
  6. Bake Bake one sheet at a time for 1 to 3 minutes. Flip it once the first side sets. It is ready when the surface blisters. A short bake stays soft. A longer bake dries into a crisp sheet.
  7. Cool To keep them soft, stack the sheets while they are warm. To keep them crisp, leave them on a rack until they are dry and brittle.
